claims.title: Inference requests may be readable across the public-to-gateway boundary if transport encryption is absent
claims.description: `flow:entity:calling-service>process:inference-gateway>submit-inference-request` crosses from `entity:calling-service` in the public-internet zone to the internet-facing `process:inference-gateway` and carries end-user text tagged `pii`. Its `encryption_in_transit` is unknown. If that attribute resolves to no effective transport encryption, an on-path observer between the calling service and gateway can intercept inference requests and read end-user text. Second-order, captured prompts can expose customer context that is subsequently forwarded by `flow:process:inference-gateway>process:model-server>forward-request` and retained in `store:inference-log`.

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium and conditional on the unknown transport-encryption attribute: the public-to-serving-edge crossing gives attackers a path to target, but they must obtain an on-path position. Impact is medium because the flow carries `pii` end-user text to `process:inference-gateway` and the gateway records requests and responses.

mitigations.detail: Set verified TLS 1.2+ for `flow:entity:calling-service>process:inference-gateway>submit-inference-request`; use mutual TLS where the calling services can support client identities.
Avoid forwarding or retaining raw end-user text unless required, and redact sensitive fields before they reach logging.

claims.title: Gateway-to-model requests may be readable on the serving-to-model-network hop
claims.description: `flow:process:inference-gateway>process:model-server>forward-request` crosses from `process:inference-gateway` into `process:model-server`'s model network, carries inference request payloads tagged `pii`, and has unknown `encryption_in_transit`. If transport protection is absent or ineffective, an attacker able to observe this boundary-crossing path can intercept customer request payloads. The intercepted content is also the input used by `process:model-server` when it reads customer features from `store:redis-feature-store`, helping an attacker correlate prompts with customer data in later attacks.

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium and conditional because observing the serving-edge-to-model-network crossing requires a network foothold, while the flow's encryption state is unverified. Impact is medium because the flow carries `pii` inference payloads into `process:model-server`.

mitigations.summary: Encrypt and authenticate the internal inference hop
mitigations.detail: Use mTLS for `flow:process:inference-gateway>process:model-server>forward-request` so payload confidentiality and both service identities are verified across the boundary.
Pass opaque references or minimized request features where the model server does not need the original end-user text.

claims.title: Model artifacts may be intercepted while the model server loads them from the registry
claims.description: `flow:process:model-server>store:model-registry-bucket>load-artifact` transfers model artifacts from `store:model-registry-bucket` to `process:model-server`, but its `encryption_in_transit` is unknown. If the object-storage connection lacks effective transport encryption, an attacker with an observation point in the model network can intercept and read proprietary model artifacts during startup. The disclosed artifact can enable offline model extraction, architecture analysis, and more targeted attacks against the serving path.

severity.justification: Likelihood is low and conditional on the unknown encryption state because the attacker needs a position on an internal model-network path. Impact is medium because the flow exposes the business-critical model artifact held by `store:model-registry-bucket`.

mitigations.summary: Require TLS for registry artifact downloads
mitigations.detail: Configure and verify TLS for `flow:process:model-server>store:model-registry-bucket>load-artifact`, including certificate validation by `process:model-server`.

mitigations.summary: Use artifact access controls and encrypted artifact packaging
mitigations.detail: Restrict artifact retrieval to the model-server identity and encrypt especially sensitive model packages before storage.

claims.title: Customer features may be intercepted between the model server and Redis
claims.description: `flow:process:model-server>store:redis-feature-store>read-features` carries per-customer account age and spend-band data tagged `pii` and `financial` from `store:redis-feature-store`; its `encryption_in_transit` is unknown. If the Redis connection is not effectively encrypted, an attacker observing the model-network path can intercept feature reads and associate customer financial characteristics with inference activity. Those correlations can then be used to target customers or to infer sensitive attributes from later model requests.

quotes.text: The features include account age and spend bands per customer.

severity.justification: Likelihood is low and conditional because an attacker must gain a model-network observation point and the flow's encryption is unverified. Impact is high because `store:redis-feature-store` is confidential and holds per-customer `pii` and `financial` features, allowing corpus-scale disclosure over repeated reads.

mitigations.detail: Enable verified TLS for `flow:process:model-server>store:redis-feature-store>read-features` and authenticate the Redis endpoint to the model server.

mitigations.summary: Limit feature content in inference requests
mitigations.detail: Fetch only the feature fields required for each inference and avoid exposing stable customer identifiers in the transport payload.

claims.title: Raw prompts and responses may be intercepted on the gateway logging path
claims.description: `flow:process:inference-gateway>store:inference-log>write-request-log` sends raw prompts and model responses from `process:inference-gateway` to `store:inference-log`, with unknown `encryption_in_transit`. If this logging connection is not protected in transit, an attacker observing it can intercept the full debug record, including end-user-supplied prompt content and model output. Second-order, one observation point can collect data from every gateway request rather than from one caller session.

quotes.text: The gateway writes every request and response into an inference log in BigQuery, for debugging.
That means raw prompts, which sometimes carry whatever the calling team's users typed.

severity.justification: Likelihood is low and conditional because the attacker needs a position on the gateway-to-log path and the connection's encryption is unknown. Impact is medium because the flow contains raw prompts and responses, with prompts potentially containing end-user-provided sensitive content.

mitigations.summary: Use verified encrypted transport to the inference log
mitigations.detail: Require TLS for `flow:process:inference-gateway>store:inference-log>write-request-log` and validate the logging endpoint identity.

mitigations.summary: Redact raw prompt and response logging
mitigations.detail: Tokenize or redact sensitive prompt fields at `process:inference-gateway` and capture only debugging fields needed for operations.

claims.title: Model artifacts may be intercepted while engineers publish them to the registry
claims.description: `flow:entity:ml-engineer>store:model-registry-bucket>publish-artifact` sends model artifacts to `store:model-registry-bucket`, but its `encryption_in_transit` is unknown. If the publishing connection lacks effective encryption, an attacker with a network observation position can intercept and read proprietary artifacts while ML engineers upload them. The copied artifact can then be analyzed offline to improve attacks against `process:model-server` or duplicate the model outside the environment.

quotes.text: ML engineers publish new model artifacts to the registry bucket.

severity.justification: Likelihood is low and conditional because interception requires a position on the engineer-to-registry path and transport encryption is unverified. Impact is medium because the transferred artifacts are business-critical data in `store:model-registry-bucket`.

mitigations.detail: Require certificate-validated TLS for `flow:entity:ml-engineer>store:model-registry-bucket>publish-artifact` and use authenticated publishing clients.
Package high-value model artifacts with envelope encryption so an intercepted upload is not directly usable.

claims.title: A registry storage copy may disclose model artifacts if encryption at rest is absent
claims.description: `store:model-registry-bucket` holds business-critical model artifacts and has `encryption_at_rest` set to unknown. If that unknown resolves to unencrypted storage, an attacker obtaining an operational copy of the bucket's media, snapshot, backup, or decommissioned storage can read model artifacts without using `process:model-server`'s service account. The copied artifacts enable offline analysis and targeted attacks against the model-serving environment. This is conditional on the unresolved at-rest encryption attribute, not an assertion that the bucket is unencrypted.

quotes.text: The model server loads model artifacts from a model registry bucket at startup.

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium and conditional on the unknown at-rest control: obtaining a storage copy requires access to operational media or exports, but no live application credential is needed if encryption is absent. Impact is medium because the bucket contains business-critical model artifacts.

mitigations.summary: Verify and enforce registry encryption at rest
mitigations.detail: Establish the encryption posture of `store:model-registry-bucket` and require managed-key or customer-managed-key encryption for the bucket, snapshots, exports, and backups.
Limit bucket export, snapshot, and key-use permissions to dedicated operational identities and audit those operations.

claims.title: A Redis storage copy may disclose confidential customer financial features
claims.description: `store:redis-feature-store` is classified confidential, holds `pii` and `financial` data, and has unknown `encryption_at_rest`. If at-rest encryption is absent, an attacker who obtains a Redis persistence file, snapshot, backup, or decommissioned volume can read account age and spend bands directly, bypassing `process:model-server` and any live Redis access path. A single copy can expose features for all customers represented in the store, enabling customer profiling and targeted fraud or social engineering. This draft is conditional on the unresolved `encryption_at_rest` value.

quotes.text: The features include account age and spend bands per customer.

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium and conditional because a storage copy must be acquired, but unencrypted media can be read without a live Redis credential. Impact is high because `store:redis-feature-store` is confidential and stores per-customer `pii` and `financial` information.

mitigations.summary: Encrypt Redis data and every operational copy at rest
mitigations.detail: Verify and enforce encryption at rest for `store:redis-feature-store`, including persistence files, snapshots, backups, and replicas, with keys unavailable to ordinary storage operators.
Apply retention limits and minimize persisted customer features so a recovered copy contains fewer sensitive records.

claims.title: An inference-log storage copy may disclose raw user prompts if at-rest encryption is absent
claims.description: `store:inference-log` retains every request and response, including raw prompts, and its `encryption_at_rest` value is unknown. If the BigQuery-backed log is unencrypted at rest, an attacker holding an exported copy, backup, snapshot, or underlying storage media can read accumulated prompt and response records without calling `process:inference-gateway`. Because the gateway logs every request, the copy can aggregate content across calling teams and expose whatever end users entered. This is conditional on the unverified at-rest encryption state.

quotes.text: The gateway writes every request and response into an inference log in BigQuery, for debugging.
That means raw prompts, which sometimes carry whatever the calling team's users typed.

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium and conditional on the unknown at-rest encryption state: a copied export or storage artifact is required, but it can be read without a gateway credential if unencrypted. Impact is medium because the store aggregates raw prompts and responses from every request, and prompts can contain user-entered sensitive content.

mitigations.summary: Verify encryption for the inference log and exports
mitigations.detail: Establish and enforce encryption at rest for `store:inference-log`, including query exports, backups, and any copied datasets.
Redact or tokenize prompt content at `process:inference-gateway`, enforce strict retention, and restrict access to log datasets as tightly as the originating request data.

claims.title: Code in the model server can read registry artifacts through its service account
claims.description: `process:model-server` reads `store:model-registry-bucket` through `flow:process:model-server>store:model-registry-bucket>load-artifact`, using its own service account. An attacker who gains code execution in `process:model-server` can use that existing reader identity to read model artifacts through the normal registry interface. This is distinct from a storage-copy threat: at-rest encryption does not prevent an authorized model-server session from receiving the artifact. The disclosed model can be copied for offline analysis and used to tailor later attacks on the inference-serving path.

quotes.text: It uses its own service account for that.

severity.justification: Likelihood is low because the attacker must first run code in internal `process:model-server`, whose exposure is unknown. Impact is medium because the service account can retrieve the business-critical model artifacts in `store:model-registry-bucket`.

mitigations.detail: Limit the model-server service account to only the specific approved artifact versions it must load and deny listing or broad object reads.
Use workload identity hardening and alert on unusual artifact downloads by `process:model-server`, especially bulk or version-enumeration reads.

claims.title: An internal foothold may read all Redis customer features if Redis has no effective client authentication
claims.description: `flow:process:model-server>store:redis-feature-store>read-features` reads confidential `pii` and `financial` customer features from `store:redis-feature-store`, while its `authentication` is unknown. The source specifically states that Redis has no password, but that alone does not settle whether another client-authentication mechanism exists. If the unresolved authentication attribute means no effective client authentication, an attacker with a foothold in the model network can connect to Redis and read account age and spend bands for customers directly. The result enables corpus-scale profiling and targeted attacks, without needing to compromise `process:model-server`.

quotes.text: Redis has no password on it; it is only reachable inside the model network.
The features include account age and spend bands per customer.

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium and conditional on the unknown authentication state: the store is stated to be internal, so an attacker needs a model-network foothold, but a lack of effective client authentication would make reads straightforward. Impact is high because `store:redis-feature-store` is confidential and contains per-customer `pii` and `financial` features.

mitigations.detail: Configure Redis to require a dedicated, least-privilege authenticated identity for `process:model-server`; do not rely on internal network reachability or the absence of a password alone.
Allow Redis connections only from the model-server workload identity and network path, and monitor or block scan, enumeration, and bulk-read behavior.
